claims.text: A League City resolution authorized an agreement with Flock Safety to lease 42 automated license plate reader cameras.

claims.text: The original Flock Safety lease ran over two years at a cost not to exceed $233,400.
claims.quote: cameras over a two-year period in an amount not to exceed $233,400 (Chief of Police)

claims.text: The council approved the first Flock lease on its consent agenda on December 20th, 2022, as Resolution No. 2022-185.
claims.quote: Approved on the Consent Agenda - Resolution No. 2022-185

claims.text: On December 12th, 2023, the council approved Resolution No. 2023-197, an updated and restated five year Flock agreement.
claims.quote: Resolution No. 2023-197 authorizing an updated and restated five (5) year

claims.text: The 2023 agreement with Flock Group, Inc covers the lease of seventy automated license plate reader cameras.

claims.text: Ordinance No. 2026-27 orders a special election in League City on Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026.
claims.quote: ordering a Special Election for the City of League City, Texas, on Tuesday, November 3, 2026,

claims.text: The proposition concerns the police department's continued use of license plate reader cameras at fixed locations on public roadways for law enforcement purposes.
claims.quote: cameras at fixed locations on public roadways for law enforcement purposes

claims.text: The council approved Ordinance No. 2026-27 on first and final reading on August 11th, 2026.

claims.text: On September 22nd, 2026, the council approved on first reading Ordinance No. 2026-39, creating a Citizen Data Privacy Committee.

claims.text: The committee is to oversee the city's Flock Safety license plate reader system.
claims.quote: to provide oversight of the City’s Flock Safety automated license plate reader system

claims.text: An amendment at first reading moved the Mayor and City Auditor to ex officio members of the committee.

claims.text: The second reading item states the council approved first reading 8-0-0 on September 22nd, 2026, with an amendment.

rejected.finding: 55 Flock cameras attributed to the city's Flock transparency portal
rejected.reason: The sentence carrying the 55 gives no attribution in its text, the count is only hyperlinked to the portal, and the portal itself sits behind a challenge wall. Kept as a Tribune count (c30).

rejected.finding: Galveston County ballot wording and Election Day polling hours
rejected.reason: galvestonvotes.org returned an empty body for robots.txt and its homepage, and galvestoncountytx.gov/robots.txt returned 403. Nothing from Galveston County was read. Ballot wording rests on Harris County's sample ballot (c27) and hours on Harris County vote centers (c28).
votetexas.gov and sos.state.tx.us robots files returned 403, so neither was fetched.
The tally came back only as a paraphrase and its vote rows were not fetched.

rejected.finding: The ex officio amendment passed with 8 votes
rejected.reason: The tally was paraphrased. The only stated tally is the first reading 8-0-0 in c20.

rejected.finding: The full text of Flock Safety's statement
rejected.reason: Only its attribution and a truncated opening came back exactly.

rejected.finding: Pasadena and Baytown among the five departments
rejected.reason: The names sit inside a dashed aside the tool would not return exactly. c44 carries only the trailing clause.

rejected.finding: KEDT vote count and camera count
rejected.reason: The KEDT article gives neither, and dates the vote only as Tuesday.
